method: The DiffServ field is the IPv4 type-of-service byte reinterpreted: the top six bits are the differentiated services code point and the low two bits are the explicit congestion notification field, so the DS field byte is the codepoint multiplied by four plus the ECN value, and the three-bit IP precedence is the codepoint shifted right by three. Class Selector codepoints are the multiples of eight, CS0 to CS7, which keep the old precedence bits and zero the rest; the Assured Forwarding codepoints follow AFxy = 8x + 2y with class x from 1 to 4 and drop precedence y from 1 to 3, so AF41 is 34; Expedited Forwarding is 46, Voice Admit is 44 and Lower Effort is 1. The mapper accepts a codepoint name, a name written in lower case, the alias DF for CS0, or a plain decimal value from 0 to 63, and reports the canonical name, the six-bit binary codepoint, the DS field byte in decimal and hex, the ECN bits, the IP precedence with its RFC 791 name, the per-hop behavior and a recommended IEEE 802.1p priority. Values that are not one of the standard codepoints are reported as unassigned rather than assigned a guessed PHB or priority, because the code point space is only partly standardised. The 802.1p column is a conventional enterprise pairing, not a standard: switches may trust, rewrite or ignore the priority code point under their own policy, and DSCP remains the marking that selects a queue across routed hops, so the page states that the local configuration is authoritative. The reverse lookup lists the named codepoints that the same table pairs with a chosen priority. Blanks, words that are not codepoints, hexadecimal input, exponent notation, values outside 0 to 63, malformed AF and CS names and invalid ECN selections are refused with the field named, rather than silently coerced. The tool maps markings only: it does not police, shape, remark, measure or generate traffic, and it does not model vendor-specific queue assignments. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: RFC 2474, Definition of the Differentiated Services Field (DS Field) in the IPv4 and IPv6 Headers: six DSCP bits plus two currently unused bits, class selector codepoints as multiples of eight.
RFC 2597, Assured Forwarding PHB Group: four classes and three drop precedences, encoded as AFxy = 8x + 2y.
RFC 3246, An Expedited Forwarding PHB: the recommended Expedited Forwarding codepoint is 46 (101110).
IEEE 802.1Q, Bridges and Bridged Networks: the three-bit Priority Code Point in the VLAN tag, and the independence of layer-2 priority from the layer-3 DSCP.
RFC 3168, The Addition of Explicit Congestion Notification to IP: the two low bits of the DS field carry Not-ECT, ECT(1), ECT(0) and CE.
RFC 5865, A Differentiated Services Code Point for Voice Admit (44), and RFC 3662, A Lower Effort Per-Domain Behavior (1).
